title: Error card
description: One error message Nyx is likely to hit. Reached by pasting the error into Identify, so `patterns` is what makes the card findable and must match real terminal output rather than an idealized version of it.

language.description: The language or tool that emits it. Omit for shell and git errors that belong to no language.

sample.description: The real message, copied verbatim from a real terminal including surrounding noise. Idealized samples do not match what she pastes.

patterns.description: Regexes matched against pasted text. Anchor on the stable part: the error class and the fixed wording. Never match on paths, line numbers, or version strings, which vary per machine.

means.description: What actually went wrong, in plain language, without the fix. Separated from the fix on purpose: understanding the cause is what stops it recurring.

category.description: not-found errors (command not found, No module named, ENOENT) mean something is missing or a path is wrong, and are cheap. broke-at-runtime errors mean the code hit a case it did not expect, and need an actual change. Nyx should learn to sort them at a glance.

fix_ladder.description: Ordered cheapest-and-most-likely first. She works down until it stops.

why.description: What this step assumes the cause is. She should know which hypothesis she just tested.

if_none_worked.description: What to paste into the agent, and what to include that she would otherwise trim off. The parts she would trim are the parts the agent uses.
